company: Atlantic Lithium Limited (AIM: ALL, ASX: A11, OTCQX: ALLIF)
location: Immediately north of Saltpond, Mfantseman Municipality, Central Region, Ghana; ~100km SW of Accra; on the N1 Accra-Cape Coast-Takoradi highway, ~110km east of Takoradi port (p5)

fx_assumption.note: Not disclosed. All figures in US$; capex prices quoted in other currencies were converted at unstated 'agreed Project exchange rates' (p41). Opex and capex exclude exchange-rate variations (p40, p42).

real_or_nominal: Not stated explicitly. Capex and opex are Q2 2023 US$ estimates that exclude escalation and inflation (p38, p40, p42), i.e. a constant-dollar cost basis; the document does not say whether the year-by-year price deck (Table 24, p44) or the 8% discount rate is real or nominal.

share.note: Table 1 footnote 2: asset currently wholly owned by Atlantic Lithium. Held via IronRidge Resources Singapore (100%), which owns Green Metals Resources Ltd 100% (PL3/109) and Barari DV Ghana Ltd 90% (operating company and holder of the Mankessim licence, described as a joint venture) (p7, p59). Results are on a 100% Project basis.

Earns up to 50% of the Project and 50% of SC6 offtake at market rates by funding US$17m of studies/exploration and US$70m of development; cost overruns or savings shared equally with Atlantic (p4 fn 2, p45).
Right to a 10% free carry once in production (p4 fn 2; Table 23 p43).

tonnes_Mt.note: JORC 2012 MRE by Ashmore Advisory, estimate at January 2023 (announced 1 Feb 2023); 0.5% Li2O cut-off, above -190mRL; inclusive of Ore Reserves; 440kt contained Li2O (p11-13). Table 1 (p4) mislabels the 3.5Mt Measured row as 'Measured Indicated'.

As of 16 June 2023 (Mining Focus Consultants, H. Warries); dry tonnes; from Measured + Indicated Resources inside the pit designs; 5% dilution, 95% mining recovery; 0.5% Li2O cut-off; US$1,587/t concentrate price (p21-22, p66-67).
No Proved Reserve declared; total = Probable (p22, p71).

inferred_share_of_mine_plan.note: 1.7Mt @ 1.19% Li2O of Inferred in the 27.3Mt processed (Table 10: 1,676kt of 27,321kt). Inferred feed is stockpiled for the first 5 years, then capped at 10% of plant feed; pits with 100% Inferred feed were removed. Case with all Inferred treated as waste: post-tax NPV8 US$1,404.8M, IRR 104.5% (p17-18, p22, p67).

deposit.mining_method: Conventional open pit: drill and blast on 5-10m benches, load and haul with 100-200t excavators and 90-150t trucks; contract mining under an Atlantic Lithium management team; eight deposits ~4km apart over ~8km2 (p14).

strip_ratio.note: 375.4Mt waste / 30.6Mt ore, 406Mt total movement (Table 1; Table 10 p18). Text on p17 says 375.0Mt waste and 12.2:1.

deposit.ore_type_notes: Spodumene-bearing pegmatite dykes (no petalite or lepidolite observed). Two geometallurgical types: P1 coarse spodumene (>20mm), 31.3Mt @ 1.27% Li2O, over 80% of the MRE, HLS recovery ~70-74%; P2 medium-fine (<20mm), 4.0Mt @ 1.06%, poor DMS response (7.0% to SC6, 14.9% to SC5.5), limited to 10% of the blend. Ewoyaa Main 30-60m thick (up to 100m at surface); Abonko/Kaampakrom 4-12m. Low sulphur (mean 845ppm); inert tailings; concentrates Fe2O3 <1% (p10, p13, p23-24, p68).

ore_mined_Mtpa.note: No annual mined-ore rate stated. Plant feed 2.7Mtpa (2.0Mt in first full year); total material movement 18-49Mt/yr (Table 10). Ore mined per year is only derivable (total minus waste, ~2.5-3.4Mt in full years).

total_ore_mined_Mt.note: LOM ore mined at 1.21% Li2O (p17). Processed ore LOM is 27.3Mt @ 1.22% Li2O (25.6Mt Probable + 1.7Mt Inferred; Table 10 p18).

life_of_mine_years.note: Includes Year 1 early-production phase (modular DMS from Q2 2025: ~9 months per p3/p27, '14 months' per Table 10 footnote) then ~11 years of the main 2.7Mtpa plant from Q1 2026 (p3).

mining_cost.note: LOM contract-mining average incl. mobilisation, establishment, pre-production mining and demobilisation (so pre-strip sits in opex, not capex). RFQ range from 8 contractors US$3.21-4.60/t (first 7 years, excl. establishment). Plus owner's mine management US$0.10/t mined. Equals US$432/dmt concentrate (Table 17). Pit optimisation used US$3.61/t (p15).

processing.route: Three-stage crushing to 10mm top size, then conventional two-stage dense media separation (DMS) on three size fractions (-10+5.6, -5.6+2.8, -2.8+0.85mm) with a -4mm recrush DMS circuit on coarse floats; -0.85mm fines dewatered and sold as secondary product; no flotation and no chemicals in the base case. Early production from a modular DMS plant with contract crushing from Q2 2025, ahead of the main plant (p1, p26-27).

throughput_Mtpa.note: Main DMS plant; first full year (2026) 2.0Mt then 2.7Mtpa; crushing at 70% utilisation, DMS at 85% (p18, p25). Early-production modular DMS: 600ktpa ore (375ktpa DMS feed, 50tph) (p27). Raised from 2.0Mtpa in the PFS (p1).

recovery_pct.note: Table 1 labels these 'average whole of ore recovery'; Tables 12 and 23 give them as P1 ore recoveries. P2 ore: 7.0% to SC6, 14.9% to SC5.5 (p24); modular DMS: 34.0% to SC5.5 (p43). Secondary product mass yield 17% of ROM feed (p4).

concentrate_grade_Li2O_pct.note: Two products ~50:50 by tonnage: SC6 1,792,222t and SC5.5 1,792,195t over LOM (~3.58Mt total) (p3-4).

concentrate_output_ktpa.note: No annual figure stated. LOM total 3,584kt SC6+SC5.5 over 12 years (p4). Figure 12 (p44) shows annual output only as unlabelled bars (by eye ~330-400kt in full-production years; Year 2 at 75% of nominal capacity; Year 4 low on higher P2 ore).

processing.by_products: Secondary product: DMS fines (-0.85+0.053mm), 4.73Mt LOM at ~1.16% Li2O (17% mass yield of ROM feed), sold FOB at a LOM average US$186/t (45% discount to the SC6 Li2O unit price, based on preliminary off-taker talks); credits US$878M LOM (US$245/t concentrate) inside C1 (p1, p4, p20, p38, p44). Future options, not in the base case: feldspar 500-1,000ktpa and flotation of fines/middlings for ~80ktpa of >5% Li2O concentrate (p49).

processing_cost.note: US$59/dmt concentrate; LOM US$212.2M (Table 17). Table 18 (p39, US$M/yr): processing and maintenance labour 6.8, reagents and consumables 2.4, maintenance materials 4.0, power 3.4, Atlantic labour 3.4, material handling 2.0. JORC table (p69) gives process opex incl. G&A as US$15.36/t plant feed. Early modular plant (Table 19 p39): contract crushing US$6.2M/yr (US$10.31/t), diesel US$2.0M/yr.

site_GA.note: LOM US$168.8M (Table 17). Ore Reserve inputs give G&A incl. marketing and insurance as US$6.18/t processed (p21). Table 18 (p39): G&A labour US$5.4M/yr, G&A expenses US$9.3M/yr, G&A power US$0.3M/yr.

overheads.power_source: Ghana national grid (GRIDCo transmission; VRA main generator; national capacity ~56% hydro, 44% thermal). New ~3km 34.5kV line from the Saltpond 161/34.5kV substation to a new site substation. Diesel power for the early-production modular plant before grid connection (p29, p39).

power_cost.note: Average grid operating cost; installed 8,500kW, average continuous load 4,270kW; DMS power US$3.4M/yr = US$1.25/t crusher feed (Table 18 p39); unit rates advised by ECG (p39).

overheads.workforce_camp_fifo: No camp: workforce housed in existing regional accommodation and hotels; senior management and visitors at a nearby resort (in care and maintenance; minor upgrade; contractor-operated) (p30, p68). >800 direct jobs; >400 on site at peak construction; hire-local policy, expatriates for 1-3 years then 100% Ghanaian staff targeted (p34, p37). Mine roster: two 12-hour shifts, three panels, 7 days a week (p14). No FIFO mentioned.

logistics.product_route: Concentrate and secondary product are stockpiled at site, loaded by front-end loader onto contracted 35t tipper trucks and hauled by road ~110km west on the existing sealed N1 Accra-Cape Coast-Takoradi highway to the deep-sea port of Takoradi (under 4 hours, even at peak), held in warehousing and outdoor storage near the port, then loaded onto ships; sold FOB Ghana port (p28, p39).

distance_km.note: Approximate. Tema port is 140km east and is used, with Takoradi, to import construction equipment (p5, p28, p34).

haulage_cost.note: Combined figure for the whole transport and logistics chain from site to loading onto ships at Takoradi (p39), so it also covers port handling and storage; the document does not split road haulage from port costs. Secondary product: US$32.65/dmt. LOM: US$106.9M concentrate + US$154.5M secondary product (Table 17 p38, 'selling' costs; p69 'selling and transport'). Pit optimisation earlier assumed 'land freight' of US$25.00/t concentrate (p15).

logistics.port: Takoradi (existing deep-sea port, ~110km west); Tema (140km east) also used for construction imports

port_cost.note: Not stated separately; included in the US$29.81/t site-to-ship logistics cost.

ocean_freight.note: Not given: all prices and costs are FOB Ghana port, so ocean freight is outside the model.

logistics.infrastructure_built: No rail, port or airstrip needed. The Project funds: a new plant-site access road joining existing roads and the N1 highway (p5, p28); internal haul roads (six major segments) and an alternative ROM haul road by end of Year 10 (p17); a ~3km 34.5kV line from the Saltpond 161/34.5kV substation plus a new site substation (p29); diversion of two HV transmission lines crossing the pits (~15km route, ~30km of new line) (p29); a water storage dam and a pump and pipeline from Lake Agege, 7km north (p28); tailings facilities, buildings and a communications tower (p29-31); minor upgrade of a nearby resort for senior staff (p30). Product trucking, port-side storage, fuel storage and mining services come from contractors (p28, p30-31).
logistics.notes: Haulage and port costs are not split: US$29.81/dmt (concentrate) and US$32.65/dmt (secondary product) cover the full chain from site to ship loading at Takoradi (p39). Trucking: fifty 35t tipper trucks and two front-end loaders, day-shift loading only, average 15-minute cycle times, supplied under contract by port-based transport companies, so no Project-owned fleet (p28). ACC Logistics and Bollore Africa contributed to the opex estimate (p53). A Traffic Impact Assessment is in preparation (p68). Transport is a small NPV sensitivity next to mining costs (Figure 14, p47). No ocean freight, CIF price or shipment size given.

C1_or_FOB_cost.note: C1 cash cost FOB Ghana port after secondary-product credits of US$245/t (~US$622/t before credits, derived). Covers mining, processing, transport and G&A; excludes royalties and VAT (p38, p40). Table 17 total 1,351,217 sits under a '$ M (LOM)' header but the figures are evidently US$ thousands (US$1.35bn).

AISC.note: Operating costs plus third-party and government royalties plus sustaining capital, from start of commercial production; excludes non-sustaining capital (p45).

royalties.name: Government of Ghana mineral royalty

rate.note: Ore Reserve inputs used 6.0% total royalty (p21); pit optimisation 6.2% (p15).

royalties.base: Not stated (modelled as a % rate, Table 23)

royalties.name: Third-party royalty, capped at US$2m total
Growth and Sustainability levy (listed under royalties)

state_participation.note: Government of Ghana right to a 10% free carry once in production (p4 fn 2).

fiscal.other_levies: GETFund levy 2.5% and NHIL 2.5% of goods and services costs, paid the year after cost incurred; COVID-19 HRL levy 1% on non-exempt goods and services; VAT 15% on goods and services (returns every 2 quarters post-construction; goods and services taken as 17% of opex); import duty 5% on operating consumables; withholding tax 20% on non-resident services and 8% on interest and dividends; CDA (community development) fund 1% of NPAT; marketing costs 3%; environmental bond first-year payment US$4,575,905; refining costs 0%; base case 100% equity (Table 23, p43). No fiscal stability agreement mentioned.

initial_capex.note: Upfront capex, Q2 2023 US$, +/-15% accuracy (Primero procedures), incl. US$12.2M contingency; US$173.0M before contingency; Table 1 rounds to US$185M. Includes the US$15.3M early-production modular DMS. Excludes sunk, corporate, exploration, financing, taxes, duties, working capital, FX and escalation (p42); mining mobilisation and pre-production mining are in mining opex (p38, p41). Capital intensity US$64/t of annualised throughput (p1).

breakdown.note: 14.9% of total; JORC table (p69) calls it 'Indirects - EPCM and working capex'

contingency.note: 6.6% of total capex (~7.1% of the US$173.0M pre-contingency subtotal, derived); JORC table (p69) says US$12.1M. Pricing basis of the US$173.0M: 79.0% priced, 15.8% estimated, 5.2% allowance (Table 21 p42).

sustaining_capex.note: Table 22 (p42) totals US$158.0M including US$45.8M closure. Sustaining part is dominated by land access and resettlement US$98.9M; others: plant and buildings 7.0, infrastructure and equipment 2.9, vehicles 1.1, tailings line 0.9, TSF stages 2-3 0.8, water line 0.5, sediment control 0.1 (US$M).

closure_cost.note: Rehabilitation and closure, LOM (Table 22); JORC table (p69) says US$45.7M. Environmental bond first-year payment US$4,575,905 (p43).

construction_period_months.unit: months, DFS completion (Jun-2023) to first ore in main plant (Jan-2026)
construction_period_months.note: Zero-float schedule; critical path is ESIA/RAP and the environmental permit. Table 16 (p36): break ground Sep-2024, early-plant first product Apr-2025, power on Sep-2025, main plant construction complete Nov-2025, first ore Jan-2026, first SC6 shipment Feb-2026.

capital.ramp_up: Early production: modular DMS with contract crushing from Q2 2025 (first product Apr-2025), ~450kt ore over ~9 months (Table 10 footnote says the early-production phase covers 14 months) (p3, p18, p27, p36). Main 2.7Mtpa plant: first ore Jan-2026; 2026 feed 2.0Mt, running at 75% of nominal capacity on an annualised basis; 2.7Mtpa from 2027 (p18, p44). Mine plan has a 3-5 month mining ramp-up (p67). Year 4 output dips on higher P2 ore (p44).

price.note: SC5.5 US$2,613/t; secondary product US$375/t. SC6 = median consensus forecast; SC5.5 = (5.5/6) x SC6 x 0.95; secondary product = 45% discount to SC6 Li2O unit price x grade ratio (p44). Real vs nominal basis not stated.
Headline 'conservative LOM concentrate pricing' (p1); also the Ore Reserve price (p21, p70).

price.unit: US$/t secondary product (~1.16% Li2O), FOB Ghana

discount_rate.note: Real/nominal not stated; base case 100% equity funded.

lom_revenue.note: All products, FOB: spodumene concentrate US$5,687M + secondary product US$878M (Table 25 p45).

annual_ebitda.note: LOM EBITDA US$3,798M, EBIT US$3,527M, NPAT US$2,284M (p45). Post-tax surplus cash flow is US$2,438M in Table 1 (p4; 'US$2.4bn' in highlights) but US$2,253M in Table 25 (p45).

economics.sensitivities: Figure 14 (p47): tornado of post-tax NPV8 for +/-25% changes in Li price, head grade, Li recovery, all opex, mining costs, transport, processing costs and capex (no data labels; by eye, price -25%/+25% moves NPV8 from ~US$1.5bn to ~US$0.9bn/~US$2.1bn). Text: a 10% price change moves post-tax NPV8 by 17.0%, head grade 16.5%, recovery 13.8%; among costs, mining matters most, then concentrate transport, then processing; insensitive to capex (p47). JORC table (p70): NPV8 stays positive under -25% price, an FX change, +25% opex or +25% capex. Inferred-excluded case: NPV8 US$1,404.8M, IRR 104.5% (p67).

risks_noted: Environmental permit: the only EXTREME (uncontrolled) project risk is obtaining and keeping the EP; residual MEDIUM after ESIA/RAP readiness works (p48).
Schedule has zero float; critical path is the ESIA and RAP needed for the environmental permit (p35).

Mining Lease not yet granted: needs a Minerals Commission application and parliamentary ratification (targeted Jul-2024) plus transfer of part of PL3/109 to Barari; several licence renewals in process (p7-8, p35-36).
Ghana presidential and parliamentary elections (Dec-2024) fall inside the build schedule (p36).
Land access and resettlement: US$98.9M LOM cost and a RAP required; >3,562 people within 2km of mineralisation (2020 survey); impacts on homes, crops and land (p33, p42, p70).
Cultural heritage: 33 shrines/heritage sites, some may need relocation in consultation with Deity-Heads (p33).
Inferred Resource is 6% of plant feed (1.7Mt), with low geological confidence (p18, p22).
Metallurgy: P2 ore recovers poorly in DMS (7.0% to SC6, 14.9% to SC5.5) and is capped at 10% of the blend; recoveries rely on a 0.85mm DMS bottom size and lab-to-plant factors (p23-24).
Secondary-product market: priced from preliminary off-taker discussions at a 45% discount; risk if the low-grade lithium product market weakens (p44, p49).
HV powerline relocation (two lines, ~30km of new line, major shutdown) must precede mining of Ewoyaa Main (p18, p29).
Groundwater drawdown may lower water levels in nearby settlements (rated low) (p29).
No lithium mining or processing experience in Ghana; expatriates needed for start-up and training (p37).
Risk register also covers infrastructure, logistics, electrical supply, water modelling, tailings and security; HAZID high hazards are personnel-vehicle interactions (p48).
NPV is most sensitive to lithium price: a 10% price change moves post-tax NPV8 by 17% (p47).
